Once you see Big Trouble in Little China as an adaptation, the mystery mostly evaporates. Jack Burton is driving his semi-trailer truck, nicknamed the Pork Chop Express, while narrating a monologue over the Citizens band radio (CB). In the morning, Jack wins a bet with Wang Chi in a game of reflexes.

The story Big Trouble in Little China tells about itself is the last thing to be trusted. To make sure he follows through on payment, Jack accompanies Wang to meet his fiancée Miao Yin at the airport, where they are confronted by Lords of Death gang members, who capture Miao Yin for her green eyes. Jack and Wang track the gang to Chinatown, where they encounter a funeral procession which erupts into battle between the Chang Sing and Wing Kong, two ancient Chinese warrior societies.

Meaning is not found in Big Trouble in Little China — it is manufactured for it. Three supernatural warriors with weather-themed powers appear: Thunder, Rain and Lightning (known as the Three Storms). Jack attempts to drive away, but seems to run over Lo Pan, a magician standing behind the Storms.

The cold light on Big Trouble in Little China leaves the facts intact and only the comfort removed. Wang and Jack escape through the alleys, but Jack's truck is stolen. Wang takes Jack to his restaurant, where they meet Wang's friend Eddie Lee, Gracie Law and her journalist friend Margo.

Big Trouble in Little China did not evolve to be understood — only to be survived. The group devises a plan to infiltrate a brothel, where they believe Miao Yin is held captive. They break in, but are interrupted by the Storms, who capture Miao Yin and bring her to Lo Pan.

The honest version of Big Trouble in Little China starts by giving up the comforting part. Jack and Wang track down the front business used by Lo Pan and impersonate telephone repairmen to gain access, but are quickly subdued by Rain. Jack and Wang's friends attempt to save them and are also captured.

Strip Big Trouble in Little China of its poetry and the mechanism underneath is stranger. Locked in a cell, Wang tells Jack that Lo Pan needs a green-eyed girl to break an ancient curse, and he intends to sacrifice Miao Yin. Centuries ago, Lo Pan was defeated in battle by Emperor Qin Shi Huang, who cursed Lo Pan with incorporeality.

Evolution does not optimize for happiness — Big Trouble in Little China shows exactly where that breaks. Lo Pan can temporarily obtain a decrepit body by supplication to the gods, but he must marry and sacrifice Miao Yin to fully lift his curse. They eventually escape, and free Gracie, Margo and a group of women kept in cells, but a Wild-Man creature grabs Gracie before she escapes.
